question: What primary metal is commonly used to manufacture standard surgical instruments?
explanation: Stainless steel provides the durability and corrosion resistance required to withstand repeated surgical sterilization cycles. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is knowing the specific anatomy of a surgical instrument important for the nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for counting instruments after surgery
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing new theater supplies
options.C: It ensures safe handling and proper functional use during procedures
options.D: It allows the nurse to sharpen the dull blades independently

explanation: Recognizing parts like the box lock and ratchets helps the nurse pass and handle instruments correctly and safely. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary function of clamping and occluding instruments?

options.A: To hold wound edges apart for better visibility
options.B: To secure skin edges with metal clips
options.C: To obstruct the flow of blood or other fluids
options.D: To cut through tough fibrous tissue layers

explanation: Clamping instruments like hemostats compress blood vessels to stop bleeding during surgical interventions. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: A scrub nurse organizing the Mayo stand for an upcoming laparotomy will group instruments primarily by what factor?

options.B: Date of their last sterilization cycle

explanation: Grouping tools by their specific surgical function allows the nurse to anticipate the surgeon's requirements rapidly. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which tool is classified as a cutting and dissecting instrument?
explanation: Operating scissors are designed with sharp blades specifically meant for cutting and dissecting tissues or materials. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h3)

question: How should a scrub nurse safely attach a disposable scalpel blade to a handle?

options.A: Warming the metal slot over an open flame
options.B: Sliding it on while wearing thick utility gloves
options.C: Pushing it firmly into place with the thumb
options.D: Using a needle holder instead of bare fingers

explanation: Using an instrument like a needle holder prevents accidental cuts and puncture injuries to the hands. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is a key structural feature of traumatic grasping instruments like Kocher forceps?

options.B: They feature teeth at the tips

explanation: Traumatic graspers have teeth that provide a secure grip on tough tissues, though they can damage delicate structures. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: When is an atraumatic grasping instrument preferred over a traumatic one?

options.A: When anchoring surgical drapes to the skin
options.B: When clamping thick, fibrous muscle layers
options.C: When handling fragile organs like the intestine
options.D: When securing heavy skin edges during closure

explanation: Atraumatic graspers have smooth or non-crushing jaws that prevent tearing or damage to delicate internal viscera. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of retracting instruments in surgery?

options.A: To cut through tough bone and cartilage structures
options.B: To hold back wound edges and expose the surgical site
options.C: To clamp bleeding blood vessels in deep tissues
options.D: To approximate skin edges before applying sutures

explanation: Retractors pull back tissues to give the surgical team a clear, unobstructed view of the operative area. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the main operational difference between manual and self-retaining retractors?

options.A: Manual retractors require two scrub nurses to hold them in place
options.B: Self-retaining retractors stay open via a mechanical mechanism without human effort
options.C: Self-retaining retractors can only be used during superficial skin procedures
options.D: Manual retractors are exclusively made of disposable plastic materials

explanation: Self-retaining retractors use a ratchet, screw, or spring mechanism to hold tissue apart independently, freeing up assistant hands. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which instrument is a common type of clamping tool used for hemostasis?
explanation: A mosquito clamp is a small hemostatic forceps used to control bleeding in delicate or superficial tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why do hemostatic clamps feature ratcheted handles?

options.A: To lock the jaws in place and maintain continuous pressure on a vessel
options.B: To allow the instrument to cut through tissue while clamping
options.C: To make the instrument easier to clean during the washing phase
options.D: To prevent the metal from bending under heavy surgical loads

explanation: The ratchet mechanism holds the jaws closed securely so the clamp stays attached to the vessel without manual pressure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary function of a needle holder during surgery?

options.A: To cut excess suture material after a knot is tied
options.B: To firmly grasp and guide a suture needle through tissue
options.C: To clamp bleeding capillaries in the subcutaneous layer
options.D: To retract skin edges away from the incision line

explanation: Needle holders are specially reinforced instruments designed to hold surgical needles securely without damaging them. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: Where should the scrub nurse ideally clamp a suture needle in the needle holder jaws?

options.A: Directly at the sharp point to ensure deep penetration
options.B: One-third to one-half the distance from the swaged end
options.C: At the very extreme tail end of the needle curve
options.D: Right across the delicate eye of a non-swaged needle

explanation: Clamping at this specific position provides optimal stability and prevents the needle from bending or breaking during tissue passage. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the very first step required in the post-operative processing of surgical instruments?

options.A: Placing them inside the autoclave chamber
options.B: Rinsing off gross blood and debris
options.C: Lubricating the ratchets with heavy oil
options.D: Wrapping them in sterile linen packs

explanation: Removing gross organic soil immediately prevents blood and tissue from drying onto the metal surfaces, which hinders later cleaning. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)

question: Why is regular inspection of instrument box locks and jaws necessary?

options.A: To determine the exact financial value of the tray for hospital inventory
options.B: To ensure the manufacturer's warranty remains active for ten years
options.C: To detect cracks, misalignment, or wear that could compromise function or safety
options.D: To eliminate the need for chemical disinfection prior to autoclaving

explanation: Routine inspection catches damaged or failing instruments before they cause injury or fail during a surgical procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)
